Plan for B1 sonicgrid-ingest at docs/phases/sonicgrid-ingest.md (roadmap Phase 10, new entry; Phase 6 B1 bullet updated). Unblocked: sonicgrid S0 hosted acceptance PASS 2026-09-30 (sonicgrid 551342c7). Contract coded against: sonicgrid documentation/BUGALIZER-POLL-ENDPOINT.md (e1fb2b7d).

Shape: separate asyncio poller task (BUGALIZER_INGEST_ENABLED, default off) polls projects with ingest_source set; imports are idempotent via new bug_reports.external_id + partial unique index (project_id, external_id); checkpoint in new ingest_state table applying the contract's four cursor rules literally, advanced only after the page commits; reconciliation = periodic full re-walk from no cursor (the cursor is opaque, so 'a few minutes behind' cannot be built) that does not move the forward checkpoint; imported reports enter as submitted/auto so Stage 1 + free local triage run as for an API submission. Token read from the env var named by credential_env at request time, follow_redirects=False, fixed error vocabulary, secrecy tests matching Phases 7/8. Operator surface: GET /projects/{id}/ingest, POST /projects/{id}/ingest/run (?full=true), /health ingest block (informational, not a degrade).

Arbiter decisions (Jack, 2026-09-29): D-A B1 before Phase 9; D-B reporterEmail dropped, never stored; D-C acceptance on BOWIE with the real token.

Points worth your scrutiny: the 400 -> clear-cursor rule (relies on contract rule 4 idempotency), crash-safety ordering (commit then checkpoint), the schema addition vs the contract's 'no schema change' line (which I read as project-config only), and whether the page cap + backoff are sufficient.

Reviewed the plan against sonicgrid/documentation/BUGALIZER-POLL-ENDPOINT.md and the existing project update/delete, health and queue code. The read-only pull, opaque cursor rules, 400 rewind with idempotency, additive report identity migration, and email omission are sound. The contract's no-schema-change wording is explicitly about B0 project configuration, so the report/state additions are compatible. D-A/D-B/D-C are respected. No tests run for this plan review.

Please resolve these lifecycle gaps before implementation:

1. Define resumable reconciliation state (plan sections 3-4). The proposed table contains only the forward cursor and last_full_walk_at, but a capped re-walk must resume on later ticks without changing that cursor. Specify a separate re-walk cursor plus an in-progress marker, completion rules (last_full_walk_at advances only on completion), restart/error/400 behavior, and how forward polling continues while a re-walk is in progress. Otherwise a backlog over the cap can repeatedly walk its prefix or delay new reports until reconciliation finishes. Add a reconciliation test spanning multiple capped ticks and a restart, with a behind-checkpoint report beyond the first chunk and an unchanged forward checkpoint.

2. Make config reset safe against an in-flight poll (sections 3 and 7). Currently only manual/background polling share the proposed lock. A PATCH can clear/reset ingest_state while an old HTTP request is outstanding, after which that request can recreate state with the old source cursor (and import old-source rows). Specify synchronization or a config generation check at the import/checkpoint commit boundary, covering config changes, clearing ingest and deletion; re-read config after acquiring any poll lock. Add a delayed-response test that changes/clears configuration before the response is committed and proves stale work cannot repopulate the reset state.

3. Preserve project deletion with the new FK (section 3 and Files). ingest_state references projects without ON DELETE CASCADE, while existing db.project_delete deletes reports then the project and foreign_keys is ON. Even a project that has imported zero reports becomes undeletable after its first recorded poll. Specify cascade or explicit transactional state cleanup in project_delete, covering both forward and reconciliation state, and test deletion of a polled project with no reports plus the existing soft-deleted-report path.

Also clarify section 7's auth statement: /health is currently public. State whether its ingest summary remains public or is redacted/authenticated, while retaining the existing readiness-probe behavior; require API-key tests for the new project endpoints. The free-processing claim in section 2 should be qualified by auto_fix_enabled=false, since analysis_mode=auto remains eligible for paid fixes when that global opt-in is on.

r2 addresses all r1 points in docs/phases/sonicgrid-ingest.md (revision note under Decisions).

1. Resumable re-walk (§3 table, §4): ingest_state gains rewalk_cursor + rewalk_started_at (in-progress marker). Each tick runs the forward poll first (own cap), then continues an in-progress re-walk for up to BUGALIZER_INGEST_REWALK_PAGES; re-walk pages commit imports + rewalk_cursor together and never touch the forward cursor. Completion on an empty page sets last_full_walk_at = rewalk_started_at (only place it moves). Restart resumes from rewalk_cursor; errors keep position; 400 clears only the cursor it was sent with. Tests 6/6a: capped multi-tick re-walk across a simulated restart, behind-checkpoint report beyond the first chunk, forward cursor byte-equal, new report imported by forward poll mid-re-walk.

2. Stale in-flight poll (new §3a): projects.ingest_generation bumped and ingest_state deleted in the same transaction as any ingest_source/ingest_config change (project_update). Poll takes the per-project lock, then re-reads config + generation. Every page's imports + checkpoint write (and error bookkeeping) is one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction that checks the current generation first; mismatch or missing project = rollback, nothing written, poll stops. Test 6b: held stub response while config is changed / cleared / project deleted, for success and error responses.

3. Deletion (§3): ingest_state FK ON DELETE CASCADE, and project_delete also deletes the state row explicitly in its transaction. Test 6c: polled zero-import project, soft-deleted-imports project, active-import project (still has_reports).

Also: public /health keeps readiness semantics and gains only enabled/projects/failing counts (no ids, error codes, cursors); new endpoints use require_api_key with 401/200 tests (13a). §2 'spends nothing' now qualified by BUGALIZER_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED=false.

Plan-only change; no tests run.

Approved. Reviewed the revised plan and round 2 submission against the round 1 findings. Separate persisted reconciliation position/in-progress state, forward-first scheduling, transactional generation checks for imports/checkpoints/error writes, and deletion cleanup resolve all three blockers. The added restart, delayed-response, deletion and auth scenarios provide concrete implementation acceptance criteria. Public health aggregation and the conditional auto-fix cost statement resolve the two clarifications. D-A/D-B/D-C remain respected; no tests run for this plan-only review.

Non-blocking editorial cleanup during implementation: Scope item 7 still promises a per-project /health line, and Risks still says malformed_response appears there; align both with section 7's aggregate-only public health contract. In test 6, assert an unchanged forward cursor in the behind-checkpoint-only scenario; the separate newly-added forward report scenario should advance that cursor normally. Apply failure backoff at the whole-tick level so a successful forward page does not erase a repeated reconciliation failure before its counter can increase.
